newsitem.title: CYPRUS: East Mediterranean residents rocked by earthquake.
newsitem.headline: East Mediterranean residents rocked by earthquake.

text.p: Screaming residents injured themselves as they scrambled to evacuate shaking buildings on Wednesday when a powerful tremor rocked the east Mediterranean.
The earthquake, which hit at 4.11 p.m. (1311 GMT) measured between 6.2 and 6.5 on the Richter scale, Cypriot seismologist Kyriakos Solomis told Reuters.
"Its epicentre was 40 km (25 miles) south-west of Cyprus in the Paphos area," Solomis said.
The U.S. National Earthquake Information Centre in Golden, Colorado, reported the quake measured 6.4 on the Richter scale.
Cyprus police said some panicked residents of Paphos in the south-west of the island were hurt as they rushed to leave trembling buildings.
There was minor damage to buildings in Paphos and the nearby port city of Limassol. Landslides were also reported in south-west Cyprus.
"All the people ran out into the streets in panic. Some were screaming and they are scared of further tremors," one witness said in northern Cyprus.
The tremor was also felt in Israel, Lebanon, Syria, Turkey and Egypt.
More than 500 people died and hundreds were hurt and left homeless when a strong earthquake hit Egypt on October 12, 1992. Most injuries occurred when badly constructed buildings collapsed.
The tremor was felt in the Turkish provinces Antalya, Adana, Konya, Izmir and Aydin but there were no reports of any damage.
In Cyprus, Wednesday's tremor lasted about a minute and telephone lines were jammed as residents sought information on the tremor and checked that friends and relatives were unharmed.
There were also a series of minor tremors.
Cyprus Radio's Paphos correspondent reported:"People in the commercial district ran into the streets. Drivers left the motors in their cars running and abandoned them."
The Paphos area was hit by an earthquake meauring 5.2 on the Richter scale in February 1995. Two elderly people were killed when their house collapsed.
In 1953, 64 people were killed when an earthquake hit Paphos.
